messages:
maria: noticed a weird breadcrumb in console after switching orgs quickly — showed a project from the previous org for ~2s then corrected :thinking:
shane: ugh, can you repro? steps?
maria: repro steps: open org A, click project list, rapidly switch to org B via quick-switch, open side panel -> sometimes panel shows org A project name but ID belongs to B (saw it in the URL)
elaine: that sounds like prefetch/cached descriptor not being invalidated on org change. which service owns the breadcrumb index?
maria: believed to be prefetchauth -> indexer writes a small breadcrumb cache keyed by user-session
nate: quick questions: are we sure the ID in the UI was B and name A? or were both mismatched?
maria: name displayed was A, hover tooltip had A, but panel details API returned B JSON. So display layer rendered stale name from local cache while backend returned correct entity
kevin: likely KV keying issue. we used user-session key + last-prefetch-timestamp. if quick switch happens, we might not evict/refresh name entries because we check timestamps with 1s granularity. race window there
shane: can we log cache hits with org header? add telemetry dimension X-Org/Org-ID to caches, so we can see cross-org hits. right now telemetry just logs cache_hit=true without org context
elaine: agree. quick diagnostic: add a one-off rollout that stamps events with header: `X-Org-ID` -> then query logs for cache_hit && different org in response
nate: small repro patch: in UI, before rendering breadcrumb, validate name vs /projects/:id API name; if mismatch, show loading skeleton for 200ms then re-render. cheap stopgap.
kevin: patch idea for runtime: make cache keys include org id + route-context. but careful: that increases cardinality. maybe use a two-level cache: global index -> org-scoped names.
maria: i can ship the UI guard. pushing a tiny change to show skeleton when name != backend name. reduces user-facing confusion while we fix server side
shane: ops ask: does this imply sensitive leakage? i.e., could an org A project name ever be shown to a B user long enough to be captured by screenshots, audit logs, etc?
kevin: worst case yes for a fleeting UI render. backend never serves A's private payload to B — only the display string from client cache. still a data exposure risk albeit low, we should treat as bug
elaine: action items: 1) kevin to propose cache key change + cost estimate, 2) shane to add telemetry dimension, 3) maria to ship UI guard, 4) nate to draft a small e2e test for rapid org switch.
shane: i'll open a telemetry PR in a few hrs. also adding an alert: any spike in cross_org_cache_hits > 0 should page oncall for now.
ate: for e2e i'll simulate browser localstore + prefetch timing. will add to flaky tests so we can capture regression windows.
maria: deployed UI guard to canary (canary-02) — deploy-bot: deploy canary-02 to eng-platform complete :white_check_mark:
kevin: starting cache key proposal doc, thinking: key = user_id|org_id|entity_type|entity_id|schema_version. this isolates cross-org collisions. downside: 3x cache memory. i'll post numbers
elaine: also check rollout UX: our canary rollout uses affinity cookie that we set before clearing old cache; maybe we accidentally keep old cookie for 500ms during rollout which can surface old entries.
shane: good catch. add cookie expiry sync to rollout script.
maria: thanks all — keeping thread here so oncall can follow. tagging @shane for telemetry PR when ready :eyes:
shane: noted, will ping once logs show a drop in cross-org hits.
kevin: ETA on prod-safe cache change: discussing with infra, might be next week if memory budget is ok. will post numbers soon.
maria: last note — filed internal bug tracker: BUG-1247 with repro gif attached. linking here: https://internal.redwood/bugs/1247
shane: thanks. closing action list in 48h unless new findings. :thumbsup:
